My Pi 5 home server build log

I spent a weekend turning a Raspberry Pi 5 into a small home server with an SSD. These are my notes for anyone trying the same thing on their own desk.

The board requires a 5V 5A USB-C power supply to deliver full current to USB peripherals. I learned this the hard way when my external drive kept disconnecting during large copies.

Active cooling is recommended for sustained workloads because the processor throttles at 85 degrees Celsius. With the official active cooler my temperatures stayed far lower during compile jobs.

In my testing, an NVMe drive on the Raspberry Pi 5 achieves sequential reads of about 450 MB/s in PCIe Gen 2 mode. That is still much faster than the microSD card I was using before this upgrade.

Overall the build works well and runs quietly in a cupboard. I will post an update after a month of continuous uptime with the services I plan to run on it.
